newsitem.title: USA: Orange County, Calif, finances are improved-report.
newsitem.headline: Orange County, Calif, finances are improved-report.

text.p: Orange County, California's financial position has improved and new credit and debt management policies are in place one year after the county emerged from bankruptcy, A.G. Edwards & Sons Inc said.

"Overall, we believe Orange County has made significant progress in its budget process and financial position, some of which is due to the slowly improving economy," A.G. Edwards said in a municipal research report on the county.
Orange County's undesignated fund balance of $67 million in 1996 represents an adequate 4.7 percent of general fund revenues, according to the report.
As of June 30, 1996, the county's combined direct debt totaled about $1.7 billion, a moderately low level for a county of 2.6 million people, the report said.

The county has also adopted a credit and debt management policy that is designed to reduce the county's debt levels and boost its credit standing on Wall Street. A.G. Edwards said it viewed these new policies "positively."
Despite the gains made over the last 12 months, A.G. Edwards said an investment grade rating in the BBB range is still warranted in Orange County's case.

The county's senior management team and the Board of Supervisors must develop a track record before a solid investment grade general obligation bond rating in the single-A range can be obtained, the report said.
Orange County shocked Wall Street in December 1994 when it descended into bankruptcy due to disastrous interest rate bets made by its once-respected treasurer, Robert Citron.

Last June -- after bringing in new leadership, slashing its budget and a launching a massive legal offensive against giant investment firms and other finance professionals -- the county emerged from bankruptcy.
